extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, ombuds, standards editors, and readers interested in media ethics and newsroom accountability
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of newsroom failures in the Claas Relotius fabrication case with recommendations for editorial practice, documentation, transparency, and institutional safeguards to prevent future forgeries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and verifiability of research
rubrics_metrics.description: The lack of transparency and verifiability of research 'does not allow readers to understand the background and environment in which a text is created.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make research processes visible so readers can grasp how material was obtained and assessed; adopt newsroom practices that enable external or internal scrutiny of reporting provenance and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive, verifiable documentation by reporters
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Reporters must also document their research more comprehensively and more verifiably.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require reporters to keep and submit verifiable records of interviews, sources, dates, locations, and documents; strengthen documentation standards so invented persons/places/documents cannot be passed off as real.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strong culture of error and mutual verification
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'weakly developed culture of error in the reporter’s department, which misinterprets mutual control as mistrust.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster an environment where checking colleagues’ work is normal and constructive, encourage admission and correction of mistakes, and remove stigma around internal scrutiny so mutual control is not seen as personal distrust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overvaluation and dramaturgy of reportage
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'overvaluation of the genre of reportage ... tempts to dramaturgical compositions, embellishments and – as in the Relotius case – to invention.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious of treating literary or dramatic writing values as a substitute for factual rigor in reportage; evaluate reportage on verifiability as well as craft, and discourage embellishment that cannot be independently confirmed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Robust independent fact-checking and documentation departments
rubrics_metrics.description: Even outlets with 'extensive documentation department[s] that checked every text' can be deceived if systems over-trust individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure documentation/fact‑checking units have independent authority and sufficient resources; design workflows that cross-check reporters’ claims against primary evidence and avoid single-person gatekeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutinize incentive structures (awards, praise) that reward sensationalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizers and juries of journalism awards had to ask themselves why they repeatedly awarded Relotius’s texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamine internal and external reward systems that may incentivize sensational, unverifiable storytelling; cultivate evaluation criteria for awards and promotion that prioritize accuracy and transparent sourcing, not just narrative impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership commitment to openness, reappraisal, and accountability
rubrics_metrics.description: A change of editors-in-chief made it 'easier ... to decide in favor of openness and consistent reappraisal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial leadership should publicly commit to transparency, set the tone for internal investigations, support reforms, and enable independent review when misconduct is suspected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional complaint and ombudsman mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: To ensure readers’ doubts are followed up, 'an ombudsman’s office was created at SPIEGEL' to follow up on tips consistently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create independent complaint/ombudsman offices or procedures that investigate reader tips and concerns, provide clear channels for reporting, and publish findings or corrective actions where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforceable rules and consequences to deter fabrication
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Faking has become much more costly' under new, stricter rules for research, documentation and texts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt concrete rules for documentation and verification and enforce them with clear consequences for violations to raise the cost of fabrication and deter misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and rebuild reader trust through demonstrable rectitude
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Without trust in the rectitude of the editorial offices ... a Relotius case must not be repeated.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize measures that make editorial rectitude demonstrable to readers—transparent corrections, explanatory reporting on methods, and visible follow-up of allegations—to preserve credibility when full verification is not possible for the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt reporting practices to a harsher misinformation environment
rubrics_metrics.description: In a globalized misinformation environment (pandemic conspiracy movements, manipulation), 'for media committed to reality and truthfulness, the struggle to be heard in their world is probably lost' unless they adjust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize and respond to the intensified circulation of false narratives by doubling down on verification, contextual reporting, clearer sourcing, and proactive communication about methods to help audiences distinguish reliable reporting from misinformation.
